$provenance: Generated by Phase 2.4 of the desktop->web transition from the Qt sources named in 'generated_from', at commit 4bd0dc5, before sub-step 2.5 deleted them. Regenerate only by editing this file: the sources no longer exist.
generated_from: every call site of its helpers
note: describe() was only one of four a11y helpers. The other three encode behaviour that a React implementation must reproduce deliberately -- it does not fall out of putting aria-label on things. 'call_sites' is derived from the AST; 'rationale' and 'web_equivalent' are authored from the Qt docstrings, because the reasoning is the part worth keeping.

patterns.rationale: The important things this app says -- 'analysis complete', '3 datasets skipped' -- happen asynchronously. A screen-reader user not focused on the status bar would otherwise never hear them.
patterns.qt_implementation: Sets the accessible DESCRIPTION and posts a DescriptionChanged event. Qt has no live-region API. Changing the accessible NAME was explicitly rejected: the name identifies the control, so overwriting it would rename the widget on every message.
patterns.web_equivalent: A container with aria-live="polite" (role="status"); update its text content and do NOT move focus. Keep the element's accessible name stable -- the same reason Qt used description over name.

patterns.wcag: 1.3.1 Info and Relationships / 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions
patterns.rationale: QLabel.setBuddy gave Qt the pairing but did NOT reliably set the field's accessible name across platforms, so the helper mirrored the label text onto the field explicitly.
patterns.qt_implementation: setBuddy + setAccessibleName, deriving the name from the label text with the '&' mnemonic marker and any trailing colon stripped ('&Host:' -> 'Host').
patterns.web_equivalent: <label for=...> / htmlFor is sufficient on the web and needs no mirroring -- the platform gap this worked around does not exist. Keep the mnemonic/colon stripping when deriving a label from the same source strings.

patterns.status: UNUSED in production as of Phase 2.4 -- defined but never called. Recorded so its absence is a known fact rather than an oversight; DOM order gives focus order on the web anyway.
